headline: Birth of Arthur Cayley
text: The English mathematician behind Cayley's theorem, which shows that every group embeds in a group of permutations. The same idea is the model for the Cayley-type and Vagner-Preston embeddings used for semigroups.

headline: Birth of James Joseph Sylvester
text: Sylvester is credited with the formula for the two-generator case of the coin problem: for coprime $a$ and $b$, the largest number that cannot be written as a non-negative combination of them is $ab - a - b$.

headline: Birth of Samuel Eilenberg
text: A founder of category theory and author of the standard work on automata, languages and machines. The Eilenberg correspondence links varieties of regular languages with pseudovarieties of finite semigroups.

headline: Birth of Marcel-Paul Schützenberger
text: A French mathematician who worked on formal languages, automata and combinatorics on words. His theorem on star-free languages was one of the first links between finite semigroups and automata.

headline: Birth of Ferdinand Georg Frobenius
text: His name is attached to the Frobenius number of a numerical semigroup, the largest integer not in the semigroup. He is better known for work on groups, matrices and representation theory.

headline: Birth of David Rees
text: A British mathematician whose 1940 work on semigroups introduced the Rees matrix construction, one of the basic tools for describing completely simple and completely 0-simple semigroups.

headline: Birth of Alfred H. Clifford
text: An American mathematician who, with G. B. Preston, wrote the two-volume work on the algebraic theory of semigroups. It long served as the field's standard reference.

headline: Birth of Herbert Wilf
text: A combinatorialist and the namesake of Wilf's conjecture on numerical semigroups, proposed in 1978. He also wrote widely read books on generating functions and algorithms.
